Quick intro — I’m Evan (Head of Infrastructure at Greystone). We’re evaluating dedicated GPU pools for production LLM inference (customer-facing features). We have a few requirements and a couple questions up front:

- Peak throughput targets: ~12k tokens/sec aggregated across 16 concurrent model endpoints (rough average; per-endpoint spikes vary).
- Model mix: mixture of 70B-context models and a few smaller 7B models; memory sensitivity matters (KV cache).
- Contract desire: 12–18 month reserved commit with monthly invoice.

Questions:
1) We want the ability to move committed capacity between GPU classes (e.g., swap some A100 to H100 or L40S) mid-term if workload shifts. Do you support in-contract swaps and how are credits/pricing handled?
2) How do you think about perf/$ tradeoffs by GPU type for our workload (A100 80GB vs H100 80GB vs L40S)? We care about memory for KV cache and token throughput.
3) Docs we can share: I attached a short demand profile.

Can we schedule a 30-min call this week to walk through options?

Thanks,

Thanks Evan — and nice to e-meet you. High level answers and suggested next steps below. Happy to jump on a call tomorrow.

Short answers:
- In-contract swaps: We support a controlled swap mechanism. You can reallocate committed units across supported GPU families once per quarter without penalty; swaps are subject to capacity availability and a small rebalancing fee unless you take our credit/discount alternative.
- Perf/$: H100 often has best perf for throughput-dominated workloads, A100 can be comparable for memory-heavy KV workloads depending on model and sequence length, and L40S is a good cost-optimized option for smaller models or inference at lower precisions. We’ll quantify for your demand profile.

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick 30-min call to confirm peak/steady ratios and acceptable memory floor per instance.
2) We’ll send 3 pricing scenarios (balanced / throughput-first / cost-optimized) with commit tiers and swap rules.
3) If you like one, we’ll produce a short term sheet and draft SLA.

Quick pricing notes (high level) — numbers are illustrative; will finalize after profiling.

Scenario A — Throughput-first (H100-heavy)
- Recommended pool: 100x H100 80GB equivalents (can be mix of H100 HW variants).
- Expected steady tokens/sec per $1k: ~28k (highly dependent on sequence length; we assume 512 avg).
- Memory note: H100 provides best FP16/AMP throughput and strong perf with KV heavy loads; lower variability on long sequences.
- Pricing: higher baseline commit cost; offer: 18-month commit with 15% upfront credit and 20% usage discount vs on-demand.

Scenario B — Balanced (hybrid H100 + L40S)
- Recommended pool: 70% H100, 30% L40S (L40S to handle smaller models and cheaper steady inferencing).
- Expected steady tokens/sec per $1k: ~22k (mixed).
- Swap policy: quarterly swap window; up to 25% of committed units reclassified between H100/L40S with 1% rebalancing fee or by applying credits to offset capacity delta.
- Pricing: 12-month commit with 12% upfront credit and tiered discounts based on utilization.

Scenario C — Cost-optimized (L40S-heavy)
- Recommended pool: 90% L40S, 10% H100 for burst.
- Expected steady tokens/sec per $1k: ~16k; best $/token for smaller models, but higher risk for 70B-long-context models if you push sequences >1024.
- Burst policy: automatic burst to H100 when latency or queue depth exceeds thresholds; billed at burst rates.

Other notes:
- A100 80GB is still attractive if the workload is strictly memory-bound (large KV caches + very long contexts). For Greystone’s mix (70B + 7B), H100 likely gives the best end-to-end throughput with L40S as a cost-efficient complement.
- Swap economics: we can offer a credit-based swap where unused committed spend converts to credits usable for the other GPU family at a 0.9 conversion ratio (1:0.9), or a fee-based swap (1% of monthly commit per 10% swap).
- Ops: need to define canary policy for model migrations when swapping GPU families to avoid tail-latency regressions.

I can turn this into a one-pager with tables and a term-sheet for the call.

Evan —

Appreciate the thoughtful questions. Short answers and an operational plan for the call:

1) Swap staging: yes — swaps can be staggered within the quarterly window. We can apply an initial tranche (min 10% of requested swap) immediately and queue remaining tranches over the next 30 days, subject to capacity. We’ll reflect staging cadence in the term-sheet.

2) Credit conversion: conversion applies to unused committed dollars (monthly underutilization converted to credits). Credits are redeemable against other GPU-family capacity at the agreed conversion ratio; they do not convert to cash refunds.

3) Perf calibration run: we offer a 7-day calibration run for enterprise prospects at no charge for this stage (sub-1yr commits) — it requires a short onboarding walk-through and instrumentation (we’ll collect perf/latency/cost metrics). For commits >12 months, we can roll the calibration into the onboarding and credit the cost to the commit.

Proposed call agenda (30 min):
- 10m: confirm demand profile & peak vs steady split.
- 10m: walk pricing scenarios & swap terms (Priyom).
- 5m: ops/canary plan & perf calibration (Karthik / Vivek).
- 5m: next steps / term-sheet signature cadence (Marissa).

If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite for Thursday 10:30 PT and attach the term-sheet draft.

Best,
